hints: Focus on what each reagent does, acid hydrolysis first, then reduction with LiAlH4.
Reaction 1 converts the nitrile group, $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$, into a carboxylic acid group, $\text{-COOH}$, with no change in carbon skeleton.
Think about what class of alcohol you get when LiAlH4 reduces a carboxylic acid, and check where the $\text{-OH}$ ends up.
walkthrough:
**Identify reaction 1, hydrolysis of a nitrile**

Think of acid hydrolysis as adding water across the nitrile. The $\text{-CN}$ carbon becomes the $\text{-COOH}$ carbon.

$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+\text{(aq)}} \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Name molecule X**

Now count the skeleton. $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C-COOH}$ has the $\text{COOH}$ carbon as C1, attached to a C2 bearing three methyl groups in total.

That is 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid, given in the table simply as dimethylpropanoic acid. The butanoic acid names would need one extra carbon, so they cannot be right.

**Identify reaction 2, reduction to alcohol Y**

LiAlH4 is a strong reducing agent. It reduces a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol by converting $\text{-COOH}$ to $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$.

$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C-COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{C-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Classify alcohol Y**

In Y, the $\text{-OH}$ carbon is attached to only one other carbon, the quaternary carbon. That is the definition of a primary alcohol.

So X is dimethylpropanoic acid and Y is primary.

options.A: Incorrect name. 2,2-dimethylbutanoic acid has 6 carbons in total, but the starting nitrile $(CH3)3CCN$ has only 5 carbons and hydrolysis does not add carbon. The class primary is correct, but the name rules this row out.
options.B: Incorrect on both parts. 3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid is also a C6 acid, one carbon too many. Y is not tertiary because reduction of an acid gives $R-CH2OH$, where the OH carbon has only one alkyl neighbour.
options.C: Correct. X is 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid from acid hydrolysis of the nitrile, and LiAlH4 reduces the acid $R-COOH$ to the primary alcohol $R-CH2OH$, which is 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol.
options.D: Half right, half wrong. The name dimethylpropanoic acid correctly describes X, but Y is not tertiary. Students who think the bulky $(CH3)3C-$ group makes the alcohol tertiary are confusing the quaternary centre with the $CH2OH$ carbon, which is primary.
